drafts.title: Physical, tactile climate controls that can be used without looking
drafts.description: Drivers can change cabin temperature and fan speed using physical controls by feel so adjustments are possible without glancing at the center screen or taking eyes off the road.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a driving usability test (on-road or driving simulator at 50 mph), 90% of participants must be able to (a) change cabin temperature to a target within ±1°C and (b) change fan speed one full step, using only touch (no visual confirmation) within 3 seconds for each operation across 10 sequential attempts.
assumptions: Controls will be placed within typical reach and follow current BMW ergonomic standards for control location.
Usability test uses representative driver seat positions and standard driving clothes (including gloves in cold-weather scenarios).
uncertainties: Some customers may prefer purely touch-based or display-only HVAC controls; trade-offs with interior aesthetic are unknown.

drafts.title: Voice assistant recognizes common driving commands with high accuracy in real driving noise
drafts.description: While driving, customers can use natural spoken phrases to operate navigation, media, phone calls and climate without repeat attempts — the voice assistant performs reliably even with typical road and wind noise.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In mixed lab and on-road tests with recorded ambient noise up to 75 dB(A), the system must correctly interpret and execute at least 95% of a standard set of 50 common driving commands (US English, natural phrasing) across 1000 randomized trials.
assumptions: Testing uses a vetted set of 50 high-frequency commands (navigation destinations, POI search, call a contact, play artist/track, climate quick commands).
Improvements can be delivered via software updates and training data collected under representative in-car conditions.
uncertainties: Performance may vary across accents and non-native speakers; achieving 95% across all accents may require extended training data collection.

drafts.title: Reliable wireless phone charging under real-world use
drafts.description: When a customer places a phone on the in-vehicle wireless charging pad, the phone reliably charges for the duration of normal trips without intermittent drops.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a mixed-device test (representative set of current major phone models and case thicknesses up to 3 mm) across 100 randomized placements and drive profiles (including low-frequency vibrations), at least 99% of placements must maintain uninterrupted charging for a continuous 20-minute drive segment.
assumptions: Test device set includes the most common phone models in the US market at time of launch.
Customers place phones in the intended charging location; gross misuse (obstruction, wet items) is excluded from the 100 tests.
uncertainties: New phone models or thicker aftermarket cases could reduce reliability; periodic revalidation will be needed after market changes.

drafts.title: Displays (HUD and center screen) remain readable in bright sunlight and minimize glare
drafts.description: Drivers can read critical information on the head-up display (speed, next navigation instruction) and primary center-screen content (navigation guidance and media title) quickly and reliably even under direct bright sunlight.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Under a direct-sunlight test condition (~80,000 lux) 90% of participants must be able to: (a) read speed and the next-turn navigation item on the HUD within 1 second from their preferred seating position, and (b) read navigation instructions and media titles on the center screen within 2 seconds while seated at typical viewing angles, across a 20-person user sample.
assumptions: Test uses representative midday sunlight or calibrated light sources that replicate direct sun conditions.
Typical seating positions and sun angles for the US market are used in the test protocol.
uncertainties: Extreme sun angles (very low sun at sunrise/sunset) may still produce reflections that require shading or user adjustment.
Different sunglasses polarizations can affect perceived readability.

drafts.title: Include heated steering wheel as part of the cold-weather package (US market)
drafts.description: Customers who select the cold-weather (cold climate) package in the US receive a heated steering wheel as part of that package, avoiding the need to buy it separately.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In the US configurator and dealer ordering system, selecting the cold-weather package must automatically include the heated steering wheel option across all trims; verified by checking 10 random configurator outputs and 10 dealer orders showing the heated steering wheel present when the cold-weather package is selected.
assumptions: Package contents are controlled centrally and changes can be made for the US market before launch.
This change is limited to package composition and does not mandate price parity in other markets.
uncertainties: Dealer-specific derogations or legacy ordering systems could temporarily display the heated steering wheel as a separate selectable item until systems are fully synced.

drafts.title: China (CCC) infotainment certification request — out of scope for product requirements
drafts.description: Customers request that the infotainment system passes China Compulsory Certification (CCC) for sale in China.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation and certification requirements (market-specific approvals) are out of scope for these customer-facing product requirements; this needs to be handled by compliance/regulatory teams.

drafts.title: GDPR compliance for driver profiles — legal/regulatory request (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that saved driver profiles meet all GDPR requirements for data storage and handling.
drafts.scope_reason: GDPR compliance is a legal/regulatory requirement and belongs to privacy/compliance scope rather than product feature definition here.

drafts.title: Request for specific cockpit chip (Snapdragon 8295) — engineering specification (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers explicitly requested the cockpit computer use the Snapdragon 8295 chip.
drafts.scope_reason: Requests for a specific chip are engineering-level specifications (out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafts); performance expectations should be translated into customer-facing acceptance criteria instead.

drafts.title: Requests to lower base price, lease cost, include packages for free, discounts, dealer margin and financing offers — business/pricing out of scope
drafts.description: Multiple customer requests relate to pricing and commercial terms (lower base price, cheaper lease than competitor, free option packages, 30% Comfort package discount, lower dealer margins, 0% financing, subscription price requests).
drafts.scope_reason: Price, lease rates, discounts, dealer margins and financing terms are commercial and business-model decisions and are out of scope for product feature requirements in this document.
